cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Resilience patterns keep a failure in one service from spreading to its callers. In microservices a failing call is a network call that may be slow, down or overloaded, and without containment it cascades.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Set timeouts on every call. Retry transient failures with exponential backoff and jitter, only for idempotent operations. A circuit breaker (closed, open, half-open) fails fast and lets a dependency recover. Bulkheads give each dependency its own pool. Sagas use compensating actions instead of two-phase commit.

questions.q: Is it always safe to retry a failed call?
questions.a: No. It may have succeeded and only the response was lost, so retrying a charge could bill twice. Retry only idempotent operations.
So many clients do not retry at the same moments and hit the dependency in synchronized waves.
Gives each dependency its own thread or connection pool so one slow dependency cannot exhaust everything.
